There are a few things Michael Porter Jr . knows a thing or two about: shooting the rock, navigating the NBA and the lifestyle around it, religion and the Bible, and dating. When it comes to the latter, he believes modern dating faces a problem that fits in everyone's palm: smartphones and social media.
 The Brooklyn Nets star made an appearance on "The Journey Podcast" in July to discuss a range of topics, including modern relationships and dating and how technology and social media are destroying them.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "What's wrong with modern dating, I think if you take the smartphones and the social media away, you would see marriages, like pregnancies, all that, like people settling down, go way up," Porter Jr. said . "I think it boils down to literally that. I think there's so much access on this phone." 
 Social media gives access to sin 
 The possibilities for human connection have expanded with the rise of social media platforms, such as Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. With just a few taps, people can start conversations, meet new people, and over time, form relationships. However, MPJ acknowledged that this also presents a serious problem, one he believes is rooted in "sin."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Because of limitless access to technology, social media and online information, he argued that people are exposed to more temptations, including the availability of various romantic options and the ability to give in to them. And this is most especially true on Instagram, according to him.
 "I feel like these phones have so much access to sin and just lust and comparison and pride. Like, there's so much in here. I think it's as simple as that," MPJ said. "On Instagram, you literally see so many beautiful women. If you're a dude who has real access and a lot of opportunity in that area, like, if this girl's tripping, why can't I just get on this next girl? 
 How MPJ avoids this problem 
 Porter Jr. is no stranger to the culture, lifestyle and attitudes surrounding relationships among NBA players. And based on the countless stories they have shared, some have not exactly been model examples.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Social media technology and technology have only made an already complicated dating landscape even more difficult to navigate. The former Denver Nuggets, for one, does not want to be part of the problem.
 "They develop that mindset, and I don't want to be that guy, man," Porter Jr. said. "I don't want to be a dude who has all these options and can't lock in." 
 To combat this, Porter Jr. said he's experimented with going without his phone for several days, particularly while on vacation. Without the constant distraction and temptation, he becomes more present in everyday interactions and more genuinely interested in the people he encounters.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Related: "He's a little girl" – Ex-NBA player says LeBron James ruined the NBA 
 Porter Jr. wants his next partner to be his wife 
 MPJ is playing his eighth season in the NBA with the Nets. At 28, he has already won a title and is set to earn over $40 million. He now looks to build his individual resume, hoping to earn his first All-Star selection.
 Off the court, Porter Jr. remains available, but he's made it clear that he's approaching his next relationship with long-term intentions .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I don't have a girlfriend right now," he said . "But the next girlfriend I have is going to be wifey and I'm loyal to her."
